case.title: Undo puts the work order back with its old lead and in its old place
case.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}, in a browser window at least 1024 px wide.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Technicians {Technician-A} and {Technician-B} are active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role and Time Clock on.
    For example: {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C682426 Ana and {Technician-B} is ZZAUTOTEST C682426 Ben.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has three Approved work orders led by {Technician-A}, shown in that column in this order from the top: {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2}, {Work-order-3}. It also has an Approved work order {Work-order-4} with no lead technician. None has a shift booked on the Schedule. {Technician-B} is not the technician on any line of {Work-order-2}, and no line of {Work-order-4} has a technician.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C682426 Undo Place, and {Work-order-1} to {Work-order-4} are S2-37441 to S2-37444.
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Board View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
case.custom_steps:
1. Drag the card for {Work-order-2} from {Technician-A}'s column onto {Technician-B}'s column and let go.
  2. Click "Undo" on the message.
  3. Read the order of the cards in {Technician-A}'s column.
  4. Refresh the page and read {Technician-A}'s column again.
  5. Click "Tech View" in the display switcher. On {Work-order-4}'s row in the "Unassigned" group, open the "More actions" (…) menu, click "Assign lead technician", then click {Technician-A} in the list.
  6. Click "Undo" on the message.
  7. Refresh the page and look at the "Unassigned" group and {Technician-A}'s group.
  8. Click {Work-order-2} to open the work order, click ⋮ at the top right (next to "New Line"), then "Audit Log", and read the two newest "Lead tech changed" entries in the Work Order Log.
case.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: {Work-order-2} moves to {Technician-B}'s column and the message "{Work-order-2} assigned to {Technician-B}" shows, with "Undo".
  • Step 2: the message closes, {Work-order-2} goes back to {Technician-A}'s column and the message "Assignment undone" shows, with no "Undo" button. No question about scheduled shifts appears.
  • Step 3: the cards read {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2}, {Work-order-3}, from the top, as before.
  • Step 4: after the refresh the column still reads {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2}, {Work-order-3}, from the top.
  • Step 5: the dialog closes, {Work-order-4} moves into {Technician-A}'s group and the message "{Work-order-4} assigned to {Technician-A}" shows, with "Undo".
  • Step 6: the message closes, {Work-order-4} goes back to the "Unassigned" group and the message "Assignment undone" shows, with no "Undo" button.
  • Step 7: after the refresh {Work-order-4} is still in the "Unassigned" group and not in {Technician-A}'s group.
  • Step 8: the newest entry is the Undo, {Technician-B} → {Technician-A}, and the one before it is {Technician-A} → {Technician-B}. Both show your user and the time.

Slavcho Mitrov (developer), 28 Oct 2026, on how he automates this test: “a Board View drag, then Undo; and the Tech View “Assign lead technician” dialog, then Undo. Each is checked again after a reload. The Audit Log part is covered by a backend test.” The steps follow his; step 8 keeps the Audit Log check for the manual tester.

Known problem (SV-11567, in Code Review on 28 Oct 2026, fast follow; Undo is its own ticket, Chris Ward on SV-11524, 20 Oct 2026; seen on the QA branch sv11524 on 26 Oct 2026): the message has the right words but no "Undo" button, only a close (×), and it closes after about 2.6 seconds. (1) If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results say, Undo has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 81 (27 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10043, story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician from the board or grouped table); tickets SV-11522 (Tech View) and SV-11524 (Board View)

  • S4-R32: “Undo puts the work order back exactly as it was before the change: the previous lead technician (or Unassigned), its previous place in that technician’s order, and any shifts the change cleared (removed shifts come back as they were; a shift that was ended at the moment of the change gets its original end time back). Each labor line goes back to the technician it had before the change, and a line that had none goes back to none; Undo does not apply the S4-R8 line rules. Undo is itself a lead change: it records its own audit entry (S4-R9), follows the Invoiced or Paid rule (S4-N2), and shows no shift-clearing prompt. After Undo the design’s toast reads “Assignment undone”, with no Undo button on it. If Undo cannot be saved, nothing changes and the alert “Couldn’t undo the change. Move the work order back by hand.” shows.”
  • S4-R9: “Every lead-change path records one audit entry with the previous lead, new lead, logged-in actor, and time.”

Not yet checked against a build.

AUTOMATION: READY - EXPECT FAIL (SV-11567)
